title: Coefficient duality and bounded finite-cohomology complexes
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and use $R$-modules in a common universe. In the module derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], define $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ to be the full subcategory of objects $K$ with bounded cohomology and each $H^i(K)$ finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Define $D_R:D(R)^{\mathrm{op}}\to D(R)$ by $D_R(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,R[0])$, the one-object ringed-site case of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Define $\delta_K:K\to D_R D_R K$ to be the transpose of evaluation $K\otimes^L D_R K\to R[0]$ after interchanging the tensor factors by the canonical Koszul braiding. Finally, let $\operatorname{FrobDual}(R)$ abbreviate the conjunction of the following assertions: $R$ is injective over itself in the sense of [lem-sf-baer-criterion] and Artinian; ordinary algebraic $\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,R)$ takes every short exact sequence of modules to a short exact sequence in the reverse direction; for every finite module $M$ its dual is finite and its canonical evaluation $M\to M^{**}$ is an isomorphism; and $D_R$ restricts to an anti-equivalence $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$. The last phrase means there exists an equivalence whose composite with the full inclusion is naturally isomorphic to the full inclusion followed by $D_R$. The first two conditions are precisely the commutative quasi-Frobenius convention.
